Dynatec Madagascar SA Posts Stable Trade Volumes in Quarterly Metals Export

Dynatec Madagascar SA, a key player in Madagascar’s metals and mining sector, reported routine trade volumes for the second quarter of 2024, with exports broadly in line with expectations. According to data released by the company on Wednesday, shipments of nickel and cobalt remained consistent with average quarterly figures over the past year, underscoring steady operational performance at its Ambatovy facility.

Company officials highlighted that nickel exports totaled 13,200 metric tons for the quarter, slightly above the 13,000-ton average of 2023. Cobalt shipments amounted to 1,350 metric tons, matching previous quarters. “We are pleased to report stable output and timely shipments for our clients,” said Jean-Luc Rakoto, Head of External Affairs at Dynatec Madagascar SA. “This reflects our ongoing commitment to reliable supply and operational discipline at the Ambatovy site.”

The metals, primarily destined for markets in East Asia and Europe, are essential inputs for stainless steel and battery manufacturing. Madagascar’s Ministry of Mines welcomed the numbers, emphasizing the sector’s importance for local employment and export revenue. “The mining industry continues to be a stable pillar for Madagascar’s economy,” said Minister Harison Randrianarisoa in a statement.

Analysts at Toliara Commodities Research noted that global nickel and cobalt prices have remained relatively stable over the quarter, contributing to predictable trade values for exporters. “The lack of major supply chain disruptions has helped maintain smooth export flows from Madagascar,” said senior analyst Victor Andriamihaja.

Workers at the Ambatovy facility, represented by the Union des Mines de Madagascar, reported normal operations throughout the period. “We have not seen any unusual interruptions or delays,” said union spokesperson Lalao Heriniaina. 

With no significant changes in production or trade conditions, Dynatec Madagascar SA’s quarterly figures reinforce the company’s role as a reliable exporter in Madagascar’s mining industry.
